land.text: Bahrayn: Abu Sa'id al-Jannabi 'captured Bahrain's capital Hajr and al-Hasa in 899, which he made the capital of his state' (Qarmatians page)

predecessors.note: Nominally an Abbasid province; the Abbasids sent an army in 900 and lost it.

land.text: Bahrain, al-Qatif and al-Hasa: the Uyunid page says Abdullah bin Ali Al Uyuni 'defeated the Qarmatians in Bahrain' in 1077-1078, with Seljuk help; the infobox founding is 1076

successors.note: Cliopatria starts its Uyunid row in 1072 and ends the Qarmatians in 1071; the pages put the end between 1067 (Agius, via the Qarmatians page) and 1077 (infobox).

capitals.name: al-Ahsa (Hofuf)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Al-Ahsa'. Hajar, two miles away, stayed the regional capital while Abu Sa'id ruled from his palace at al-Ahsa (Abu Sa'id page); Abu Tahir 'declared the city his permanent capital' (Abu Tahir page). Coordinates are Hofuf's.

rulers.name: Abu Sa'id al-Jannabi
rulers.note: Murdered in June/July 913 while bathing; the news reached Baghdad in summer 914.

rulers.name: Sa'id (eldest son of Abu Sa'id)
rulers.note: 'He was succeeded by his eldest son, Sa'id' (Abu Sa'id page); Abu Tahir 'became the leader of the state in 923, after ousting his older brother' (Abu Tahir page).

rulers.name: Abu Tahir al-Jannabi
rulers.note: Died of smallpox in 944; the Qarmatians page infobox says 914-944 but its body says 923-944. After him 'his three surviving sons and nephews' ruled together; no list of reigns was found on the pages opened.

union.text: al-Hasa oasis with Hajar and al-Ahsa, 'Bahrain's capital Hajr and al-Hasa' captured in 899

correction.text: Cliopatria's 899 shape plus the capital oasis

keyframe_review.note: 64,923 km2 for 899-969, a coastal strip (Qatif 71%, Bahrain, Qatar, the UAE coast, part of Kuwait on the gazetteer's reckoning) that leaves out the al-Hasa oasis around Hofuf where the page puts the capital. The infobox gives no area, so no ratio. The page: 'Its greatest stronghold remained in Bahrain, which then included much of eastern Arabia' and the state 'controlled the coast of Oman'. Shape kept, the capital oasis added.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 970 shape plus the capital oasis; the Syrian ground 971-978 is contested, not Qarmatian territory

keyframe_review.note: 64,680 km2 for 970-979, the same coastal strip. In these years the Qarmatians fought the Fatimids for Damascus and Ramla (25 August 971, 5 September 971) and 'were to leave Palestine' in 978; that ground is carried by the contest events, not by this shape. Capital oasis added as in 899.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 980 shape plus the capital oasis, valid 980-1057; the Qatar and UAE coasts dropped in 980 are not explained by any page opened

keyframe_review.note: 6,700 km2 for 980-1065, down from 64,680: only Qatif and Bahrain survive. The pages opened say only that 'after their defeat by the Abbasids in 976, the Qarmatians began to look inwards' and that 'Bahrain broke away in 1058'; none explains a loss of the Qatar and UAE coasts in 980. Unverified within the page budget; the capital oasis is added and the shape is valid 980-1057 only (Bahrain leaves in 1058, see the next keyframe). Repair note 2026-10-19: Eastern Arabia, History of Bahrain and Bahrayn (historical region) were opened for the drop and are silent on 976-1000 and on 980; none names Qatar or the UAE as Qarmatian land (they give only 'controlling the coast of Oman', undated), and the only cause they give is the 976 defeat by the Abbasids. The drop stays unexplained. [orchestrator 2 Nov 2026: from/to set to 980..1057 from this entry's own 'valid 980-1057 only'; without them the compiler drew the shape for all its Cliopatria years, overlapping the next keyframe (window p1100-p1199 report)]

correction.text: al-Hasa and Qatif without Bahrain island, 1058-1065

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1058-1065: 'Bahrain broke away in CE 1058 under the leadership of' Abu al-Bahlul al-Awwam; the Qarmatians keep al-Hasa and Qatif until the Uyunid siege of Hofuf.

correction.text: al-Hasa and Qatif without Bahrain island, 1066-1071

keyframe_review.note: 6,700 km2 for 1066-1071; the same coastal shape. Bahrain had left in 1058, and the Uyunid page has the Qarmatians defeated only in 1077-1078 'in Bahrain' with the Hofuf siege, so this shape is also valid to 1071 only as al-Hasa and Qatif without Bahrain.

union.text: Hofuf, besieged by the Uyunids and Seljuk Turks

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1072-1077: Cliopatria ends the Qarmatians in 1071 and starts the Uyunid Emirate in 1072, but the pages date the Qarmatian defeat to 1077-1078 (Uyunid page; Qarmatians infobox 'Overthrow: 1077'; the Uyunid infobox says 1076). Agius, quoted on the Qarmatians page, gives 1067. The state is kept to 1077 on the infoboxes and the siege of Hofuf 'for seven years'.

region.text: Hajr and al-Hasa, with Qatif taken the same year

ledger.note: 899: Abu Sa'id al-Jannabi founds the Qarmatian state in Bahrayn. The page: he 'captured Bahrain's capital Hajr and al-Hasa in 899, which he made the capital of his state'; infobox 'Established: 899'. The pages disagree on Hajar: the Abu Sa'id page has his followers controlling 'most of Bahrayn, except for the regional capital' (Hajar, still Abbasid) in 899 and the lead has him capture Hajar in 903.
899: the Qarmatians take Qatif. 'He took Qatif in 899', and its fall alarmed Basra; 'By 899, his followers controlled large parts of the region'.

union.text: the salt marsh two days' march from Qatif

region.text: Qatif and Hajar, the ground between them where the Abbasid army was beaten

ledger.note: 900: the Abbasids send an army against the Qarmatians. Al-Mu'tadid 'in April 900 named his general al-Abbas ibn Amr al-Ghanawi governor of Bahrayn and Yamama'; 'On 31 July, in a salt marsh some two days' march from Qatif, the Abbasid army was defeated in battle'; about 700 prisoners were executed.

903: Hajar surrenders and the Qarmatians hold Bahrayn. 'Hajar was forced to surrender anew to the Qarmatians after they cut its water supply'; the Abbasid governor Ibn Banu nevertheless reported in late 903 that he had 'captured Qatif' (his own claim, as the page presents it), so the end of the contest at 903 is my reading.

903: Hajar passes to the Qarmatians. The lead: 'He captured the local capital, Hajar, in 903, and extended his rule south and east into Oman'; Hajar 'remained the regional capital' beside Abu Sa'id's own palace at the al-Ahsa oasis. The Qarmatians page dates the capture of Hajr to 899. Repair note 2026-10-19: the conquest section of the same page has Hajar 'captured, only to be lost again after the arrival of a new Abbasid governor in 901' (after the 31 July 900 victory) and then forced 'to surrender anew' in 903, so the hold on Hajar that the 899 found event gives the Qarmatians was lost and retaken inside the 900-903 contest. The same page has his expeditions reaching 'as far east as Sohar (which he briefly captured after several attempts)', with no date and no loss; no gain is written for Sohar (a 150 km circle would be larger than the whole Cliopatria shape, and nothing keeps it Qarmatian), and the Qarmatians page's 'controlled the coast of Oman' is undated.

region.text: the Ikhshidid governor's Syria and Palestine, Damascus and Ramla

ledger.note: 968: the Ikhshidid governor of Syria and Palestine becomes the Qarmatians' tributary. Al-A'sam 'defeated the Ikhshidid governor, al-Hasan ibn Ubayd Allah ibn Tughj in battle before his capital, Ramla, on 28 October 968' and 'The Ikhsidid governor was obliged to agree to an annual tribute of 300,000 dinars'; the Qarmatian forces under al-A'sam had captured Damascus. Confidence 2: the page calls it a tribute, not a vassalage, and the payer's province as the zone is my reading (the Ikhshidids have no row in Cliopatria).

region.text: the Ikhshidid governor's Syria and Palestine, Damascus and Ramla

ledger.note: 970: the Fatimid takeover ends the tribute. 'The Fatimid takeover meant the end of the annual tribute promised by al-Hasan ibn Ubayd Allah ibn Tughj' (the page gives no year for the end). The fatimid-caliphate dossier, from the Fatimid conquest of Egypt page, has the Fatimids capture the governor in May 970 and Damascus in November 970; 970 is a bridge between the two pages.

region.text: Damascus and Ramla, the Syrian and Palestinian ground the Qarmatians held against the Fatimids

ledger.note: 971: the Qarmatians and the Fatimids fight for Syria and Palestine. On 25 August 971 'the allies captured Damascus' and al-A'sam proclaimed the Abbasid caliph's suzerainty; the Qarmatians sacked Ramla on 5 September 971; they were beaten in two battles on 22 and 24 December near Ayn Shams. The 'allies' were a coalition assembled through the Abbasid caliph al-Muti': the Qarmatians, the Hamdanid Abu Taghlib of Mosul, the Buyid Izz al-Dawla, Bedouin tribes and Ikhshidid remnants. Earlier, on 28 October 968, al-A'sam had beaten the Ikhshidid governor before Ramla and the Qarmatian forces captured Damascus, the governor agreeing to a tribute of 300,000 dinars (the Ikhshidids have no row in Cliopatria).

region.text: Damascus and Ramla, the Syrian and Palestinian ground the Qarmatians held against the Fatimids

ledger.note: 978: the Qarmatians leave Palestine. 'In 978, after defeating the allies, the new Fatimid caliph al-Aziz offered an annual tribute of 30,000 dinars'; the Qarmatians were to 'recognize Fatimid suzerainty, leave Palestine, and return to Bahrayn' (other sources give 20,000 or 70,000 dinars). Al-A'sam had died at Ramla in March 977.

1058: Bahrain island breaks away. 'Bahrain broke away in CE 1058 under the leadership of' Abu al-Bahlul al-Awwam (the page's spelling). How long the breakaway held is not on the pages; no rebel dossier is written here. Repair note 2026-10-19: the Eastern Arabia, History of Bahrain and Bahrayn (historical region) pages name the leaders as Abul-Bahlul al-'Awwam and Abu'l-Walid Muslim of the Abd al-Qays tribe and say 'Around 1058' the revolt 'heralded the collapse of Qarmatian power'; none says how long the breakaway lasted, and the Uyunid page does not mention it.

1067: the Uyunid-Seljuk campaign against the last Qarmatian ground begins. The page: 'Their dynasty was finally dealt a final blow in 1067 by the combined forces of' Abdullah bin Ali Al Uyuni, with Seljuk contingents, who 'laid siege to Hofuf for seven years and finally forced the Carmathians to surrender'. Agius dates the disappearance to 1067 'after they lost their fleet at Bahrain Island'. The 1067 start and the siege length come from one page; the Uyunid page has the defeat in 1077-1078.

1077: Hofuf falls. 'In 1077-1078, an Arab sheikh named Abdullah bin Ali Al Uyuni defeated the Qarmatians in Bahrain'; the Hofuf siege is named as the decisive battle, 'with help from Seljuq Turks of Baghdad'. The Uyunid infobox says founded 1076; the Qarmatians infobox says 'Overthrow: 1077'.

region.text: al-Hasa and Qatif, the last Qarmatian ground

ledger.note: 1077: the Qarmatian state ends. Infobox 'Overthrow: 1077'; 'Descendants of Abu Yaqub Yousuf ruled until 1077'; the Uyunid Emirate replaces it in Bahrain and eastern Arabia. Cliopatria ends the row in 1071 and starts the Uyunid row in 1072.

wars.name: Abbasid campaigns against Abu Sa'id al-Jannabi
wars.outcome: The Abbasid army under al-Abbas ibn Amr al-Ghanawi (2,000 soldiers with volunteers) was defeated on 31 July 900 near Qatif (al-Ghanawi captured, then released); Hajar, captured after the 900 victory, was lost again in 901 and surrendered anew in 903; the lead has his rule extended into Oman and the body has expeditions reaching Sohar, 'which he briefly captured after several attempts' (undated, no hold written); Yamama 'was probably not placed under Qarmatian control'.

wars.name: Qarmatian raids on Iraq and the pilgrim road
wars.outcome: Raids without lasting ground: the Hajj caravan ambushed in 906 ('massacred 20,000 pilgrims'), Basra raided in 912 and from 923, Kufa raided in 927 with an Abbasid army beaten, Baghdad threatened in 928 (the page dates it 928; the Qarmatians page says the Qarmatians 'came close to capturing Baghdad in 927').
wars.note: Zones empty: nothing was held. The Qarmatians page adds that they besieged Damascus and devastated cities to the north (undated).

wars.name: Qarmatian sack of Mecca
wars.outcome: Abu Tahir sacked Mecca in 930 (the pages give no month) and carried the Black Stone to al-Ahsa; 'Attempts by the Abbasids and Fatimids to persuade him to return the Black Stone were rejected'; the Abbasids paid a large sum and it was returned in 952.
wars.note: Return date 952 from the Qarmatians page. A raid, not an occupation: Mecca was not held.

wars.name: Fatimid-Qarmatian wars in Syria and Egypt

zones.text: Damascus and Ramla, the Syrian and Palestinian ground the Qarmatians held against the Fatimids

wars.outcome: After taking Damascus from the Ikhshidid governor in 968 al-A'sam invaded Egypt in 971 and 974 and was beaten in two battles on 22 and 24 December 971 (the Fatimids had dug in at Ayn Shams) and at Jubb Umayra on 27 April 974; he died at Ramla in March 977; in 978 al-Aziz paid tribute and the Qarmatians left Palestine for Bahrayn.
wars.note: The Battle of Kufa and the loss of Hajar named in the research prompt are not on any page opened.

wars.name: Abbasid defeat of the Qarmatians
wars.outcome: 'After their defeat by the Abbasids in 976, the Qarmatians began to look inwards' (Qarmatians page); the place and the Buyid share are not given.
wars.note: No zone: the page gives the year only.

wars.name: Uyunid and Seljuk conquest of al-Hasa
wars.outcome: Abdullah bin Ali Al Uyuni, with Seljuk Turks, besieged Hofuf for seven years and ended the Qarmatian state (1077-1078 on the Uyunid page).
wars.note: Dates disagree: 1067 (Agius, Qarmatians page), 1076 (Uyunid infobox), 1077 (Qarmatians infobox), 1077-1078 (Uyunid text).

certainty.note: Desert-oasis and coastal frontiers of eastern Arabia; none is fixed by treaty or survey. The Syrian ground 968-978 is contested, not bounded.

notes: Cliopatria's Qarmatian shapes are a coastal strip and exclude the al-Hasa oasis around Hofuf, where every page puts the capital; each shape is adjusted to add it (place 'Hofuf', 60 km). The 980 shape shrinks from 64,680 to 6,700 km2 with no page opened explaining it (only the 976 Abbasid defeat and 'began to look inwards'); unverified within the 5-page budget. Dates of the end disagree: 1067 (Agius), 1076 (Uyunid infobox), 1077 (Qarmatians infobox, taken here), 1077-1078 (Uyunid text); Cliopatria ends the row in 1071 and starts the Uyunid row (uyunid-emirate, written by another part of me-08) in 1072, so the two shapes cover 1072-1077 twice if both are used. Bahrain island broke away in 1058 under Abu al-Bahlul al-Awwam: a rebel entity with no dossier. Qarmatians elsewhere: a Qarmatian ruler at Multan (Abdul Fateh Daud, Mahmud of Ghazni's expedition of 1005) is on the Qarmatians page only in passing; the Qarmatian rebellions of Iraq and Syria (Zakarawayh 901-907) are named on the Abu Sa'id page as uncoordinated with Bahrayn. Not found on the pages opened: the Battle of Kufa (977/978), the loss of Hajar, a capital called Mu'miniya, Yamama, Ray, Buyid-Qarmatian relations 973-978. The Fatimid page says the Qarmatians were paid tribute by the Fatimids (not written: it runs to the Qarmatians and no page gives its years). The 968 tribute of 300,000 dinars from the Ikhshidid governor of Syria and Palestine is written as a tributary tie (vassal_start 968, vassal_end 970 at confidence 1), from the Al-Hasan al-A'sam page. Ruler list stops at 944: afterwards 'his three surviving sons and nephews' ruled together and no list was opened. Gazetteer: all names used exist (Hofuf, Al-Qatif, Ramla, Damascus admin1, Bahrain). Repair 2026-10-19 (after review me-08-c): (1) the 903 gain of a 150 km circle around Suhar is dropped: the Abu Sa'id page says only that he 'briefly captured' Sohar 'after several attempts', with no date and no loss, and a 150 km circle (about 70,000 km2) is bigger than the whole Cliopatria shape (64,923 km2); the raid is in the note of the 903 Hajar gain, and the buyid-dynasty gain of the same circle in 972 no longer overlaps. (2) The Hajar note says the hold was lost in 901 and retaken in 903 inside the 900-903 contest. (3) The 968 tribute is now a vassal pair. (4) Three more pages (Eastern Arabia, History of Bahrain, Bahrayn historical region) were opened for the 980 drop and the 1058 breakaway: none explains the drop (silent on 976-1000, Qatar and the UAE) and none gives the length of the 1058 breakaway. (5) Cross-check from the review (the Fatimid gains of Ramla in 972 and of Palestine in 978 'from the Qarmatians' against a contest here): kept as a contest pair on purpose. The A'sam page says the Qarmatians 'remained in control of Syria' after 971 and 'abandon Palestine' in 978, but dates no holding of Ramla or Damascus (Ramla sacked 5 September 971, entered 12 March 977), so a gain and loss would invent dates; the Fatimid gains mark the winner of the contest zone.
